concepts.def: Designed to teach a moral lesson
A small world that stands for a bigger one
Society ruled and led by men

walkthroughs.body_html:
Didactic = teaches a lesson. Polemical = attacks an idea.

A Christmas Carol is didactic. An Inspector Calls is polemical. Use the precise word.

The Birling dining room is a microcosm of Edwardian capitalism.

The island in Lord of the Flies is a microcosm of society. Top essays spot these miniature worlds.

Calling a society patriarchal isn't just a label — it opens up feminist readings.

Lady Macbeth, Sheila Birling and Jane Eyre all operate inside (and against) patriarchal structures.

mcqs.q: Which word best describes An Inspector Calls?
options: didactic
polemical
allegorical
omniscient

mcqs.q: A small world that stands for a bigger one is a:
options: macrocosm
microcosm
allegory
motif

mcqs.q: Why must students distinguish the narrator from the author?
options: The narrator is a constructed voice within the text; the author is the real person who created it. Conflating them misreads irony, unreliable narration and persona.
The narrator's views are always the author's views.
The narrator and author are different words for the same thing.
Context is required because all texts are about history.

mcqs.q: Why does historical context matter when reading literature?
options: Texts emerge from and respond to specific historical conditions — context illuminates references, assumptions and arguments that might otherwise be invisible.
Context just means writing about what the author had for breakfast.
Context is required because all texts are about history.
The narrator and author are different words for the same thing.
Modernism just means literature written in modern times.
Context is required because all texts are about history.
Modernism is literature about modern technology like phones.
Experimentation with form (fragmentation, stream of consciousness), focus on subjective interior experience, scepticism toward traditional narrative and absolute truth.
